title: Handoff alignment scratch - product / eng / applied-ml
content:
Purpose:
Prepare for 30m cross-functional alignment sync: product (roadmap priorities), eng (serving runtime + infra constraints), applied-ml (model onboarding & evals). This is a scratchpad — rough bullets, things to surface, open questions, and initial action assignments.

Meeting goals (top 3):
- Agree on scope and slates for Q2 model onboarding waves (which model sizes/quantization profiles go to Dedicated vs Hosted).
- Surface any non-negotiable infra limits (GPU types, memory, latency SLO impacts) that would block Product's proposed rollouts.
- Decide evaluation gating criteria (per-prompt regressions threshold, perf delta tolerances) and who owns post-rollout regressions.

Context reminders (notes to self):
- Product wants to ship "smaller-model" cheaper tier for embeddings + chat-lite by mid-April to meet customers migrating from other vendors.
- Eng has autoscaling changes scheduled the week after; might affect Dedicated burst capacity testing.
- Applied-ML has flagged two model families that need KV-cache changes due to attention pattern differences.

Proposed agenda (30m):
1) 3m quick intros + goal statement (Harper)
2) 7m Product: target customers, KPIs, and initial model list (Maya)
3) 7m Eng: capacity constraints and rollout windows (Eli)
4) 7m Applied-ML: eval plan + gating metrics (Noah)
5) 6m Decide next steps, owners, and immediate blockers

Open questions to raise early:
- Product: what’s the minimum acceptable latency for the "chat-lite" use-case? (p50/p95 targets)
- Eng: can we guarantee quantized model parity for the 8-bit variant across both NVLink nodes and single-GPU hosts? If not, fallback strategy?
- Applied-ML: what eval datasets will be canonical for regressions? Who maintains them?
- Billing/Cost: do we need a new billing SKU for the cheaper tier or re-use existing embedding pricing? (flag to finance later)

Assumptions (call these out):
- Assume Dedicated fleet can be reserved 2 weeks ahead for canary testing.
- Assume Optimize suggestions will recommend batching changes that change p50 but improve cost; we need thresholds for acceptable regressions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: quantization causes quality regression > accepted threshold. Mitigation: fallback to float variant on mismatch; create canary with small percentage of traffic. Owner: Applied-ML.
- Risk: autoscaling rollout interferes with Dedicated tests. Mitigation: schedule Dedicated canary earlier or ask SRE to freeze autoscaling changes. Owner: Eng (Eli) — escalate to SRE if needed.
- Risk: ambiguous ownership for post-launch regressions across model/version/route. Mitigation: define on-call rota for model regressions (applied-ml primary, eng secondary). Owner: Product to formalize.

Decision points needed in meeting:
- Final model list for wave 1 (names & variants).
- Quantization profile to adopt for wave 1 (8-bit vs 4-bit hybrid).
- Traffic split for canary (1% vs 5%?).
- Blocker thresholds (e.g., >2% regression on NLU benchmarks blocks launch).

Draft gating criteria (to propose):
- Semantic regression: no more than 1.5% drop on customer-intent set (canonical set maintained by Applied-ML).
- Latency: p95 must be <= 500ms for chat-lite on Hosted API under typical load.
- Cost delta: normalized per-token cost improvement of at least 20% vs baseline for chosen variants.

Initial action items (rough — fill in during meeting):
- Product (Maya): produce final candidate model list + priority ranking by 2026-03-16.
- Applied-ML (Noah): prepare evaluation harness and canonical dataset link; run baseline regressions by 2026-03-18.
- Eng (Eli): confirm Dedicated capacity reservation calendar and whether autoscaling freeze is possible; provide node-type constraints by 2026-03-14.
- Harper: draft canary rollout plan template and share with team by 2026-03-15.
- All: quick pre-read (one pager) to be uploaded to linked_artifacts by end of day Friday.

Notes for follow-up (post-meeting):
- If we decide on hybrid quantization, schedule a 1h deep-dive with runtime team to validate kernel availability and performance variance.
- If p95 target not achievable on Hosted, identify fallback routes (regional routing to lower-latency region, smaller context windows, or model distillation).

Scratch ideas (brainstorm, keep very rough):
- "Fast-lane" config: pre-warm KV cache for returning customers to improve p95 on chat-lite without changing model.
- Lightweight monitoring check: add a synthetic trace that runs 5 prompts every 10m against canary to catch regressions quickly.
- Post-launch champion: rotate ownership across Applied-ML and Eng for 2-week windows to ensure quick triage.

Quick links / references to drop in meeting:
- Eval harness (Noah): https://internal.redwood/evals/canonical-chat-lite (placeholder)
- Linear ticket for rollout plan: RED-4126
- Runtime PR for quantization support: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/289

Personal notes / to-self before the call:
- Remind Maya to be specific about customer personas (who will migrate).
- Confirm whether Finance needs an early heads-up for a new SKU.
- Bring up SRE impact plainly — avoid surprise for Eng.

Possible attendees (proposed):
- Maya Patel (Product lead - hosted API)
- Eli Torres (Eng - serving runtime)
- Noah Brooks (Applied-ML)
- Harper Chen (Host / facilitator)
- Optional: SRE rep (TBD), Finance lead (TBD)

Tone + facilitation notes:
- Keep decisions binary where possible (pick A or B) to avoid drifting.
- Use the meeting to surface only blockers; anything implementation-heavy should be deferred to a follow-up deep-dive.
- Record a quick decision summary and post to #product-ops and attach to Linear ticket.

End of scratchpad. Will convert into a tidy pre-read if meeting confirms scope.
